name: Ethanol-water heat-flash-cool-pump train
description: Process an ethanol-water feed (40 mol% ethanol) at 25°C and 1 atm through a four-unit sequence: heat to 80°C to partially vaporise ethanol, flash-separate in a vessel at atmospheric pressure, cool the water-rich liquid bottoms to 35°C, then pump to 3 bar for downstream use. NRTL with binary interaction parameters is required for accurate VLE.
source: Bioethanol dehydration pre-concentration step. Four-unit chain exercises Cooler→Pump coupling: Cooler T_out must remain below Pump cavitation limit.
notes: Ethanol bp=78.4°C, water bp=100°C. At 80°C the feed is in the two-phase region — NRTL BIPs required for accurate y/x split. Cooler-to-Pump coupling means GlobalConsistencyPass must enforce T_out_cooler well below bubble point before pump inlet.

name: 1-Propanol-water heat-flash-cool-pump train
description: Separate a 1-propanol and water feed (35 mol% 1-propanol) at 25°C and 1 atm: heat to 100°C where both components are near their boiling points, flash-separate in a vessel, cool the water-rich liquid bottoms to 40°C, then pump the cooled stream to 5 bar for downstream processing.
source: Propanol recovery from fermentation broth. Operating near both component boiling points creates strong VLE sensitivity: a 5 K error in heater target flips from two-phase to single-phase regime.
notes: 1-Propanol bp=97.2°C, water bp=100°C. At 35 mol% 1-propanol, flash at ~100°C gives substantial separation. Strong coupling: heater T_out is within 3 K of water bubble point, so GlobalConsistencyPass margin enforcement is critical.

name: DMSO-water heat-flash-cool concentration
description: Concentrate a dimethyl sulfoxide and water feed (50 mol% DMSO) at 25°C and 1 atm: heat to 110°C to vaporise water selectively (DMSO boiling point is 189°C), flash-separate the two-phase mixture in a vessel, then cool the DMSO-rich liquid bottoms to 40°C for product recovery.
source: DMSO solvent recovery and concentration. Large boiling point spread (89 K) means water is selectively evaporated. Tests whether ParamMapper correctly targets a temperature far above water bp but well below DMSO bp.
notes: DMSO bp=189°C, water bp=100°C. At 110°C (10 K above water bp, 79 K below DMSO bp) water evaporates preferentially. Large composition difference between vapour (water-rich) and liquid (DMSO-rich) makes this a strong separation check.

name: Ethylene glycol-water heat-flash-cool-pump train
description: Process an ethylene glycol and water feed (30 mol% EG) at 25°C and 1 atm: heat to 108°C to vaporise water selectively (EG bp=197.5°C), flash-separate in a vessel, cool the EG-rich liquid bottoms to 50°C, then pump the cooled product to 8 bar for downstream glycol recovery.
source: Glycol dehydration unit in natural gas processing. Very high BP spread (97.5 K) creates near-complete water/EG separation in a single flash. Tests Pump after Cooler coupling with high-viscosity liquid.
notes: EG bp=197.5°C, water bp=100°C. At 108°C essentially all EG stays liquid. Vapour is nearly pure water, liquid is EG-rich — tests whether separation_achieved check correctly flags near-complete separation (expected rel_diff >> 10%).

name: Methane-ethane-propane compress-cool-flash-pump LNG pre-train
description: Pre-process a light natural gas feed (70 mol% methane, 20% ethane, 10% propane) at 25°C and 1 bar through a four-unit LNG preparation sequence: compress to 30 bar (temperature rises to ~175°C due to adiabatic compression), intercool to -30°C to partially liquefy ethane and propane, flash-separate the two-phase stream in a vessel, then pump the C2/C3-rich liquid to 50 bar for liquefaction.
source: Natural gas liquids (NGL) extraction. Compress-intercool-flash is the first stage of LNG production. Tests cryogenic Cooler→Vessel coupling: Cooler T_out must be between methane dew point and propane bubble point at 30 bar.
notes: At 30 bar: methane bp≈-100°C (173K), ethane bp≈-15°C (258K), propane bp≈48°C (321K). Cooling to -30°C (243K) liquefies most propane and some ethane. PR or LKP required for cryogenic accuracy. Strong Comp→Cool coupling: adiabatic compression T rise must be fully removed by cooler.

name: Propane-butane LPG compress-cool-flash splitter
description: Separate a propane and n-butane mixture (60 mol% propane, 40 mol% n-butane) at 25°C and 1 bar using a three-unit LPG fractionation sequence: compress from 1 bar to 8 bar, cool the compressed gas to 20°C to partially condense butane, then flash-separate in a vessel to recover propane-rich vapour from butane-rich liquid.
source: LPG fractionation — propane-butane splitter first stage. At 8 bar propane bubble point ≈19°C (292K), butane bubble point ≈71°C (344K). Cooler target (20°C) sits between the two bubble points, producing selective butane condensation.
notes: PR EOS required. At 8 bar and 20°C, the 60/40 propane/butane mixture is in the two-phase region. System must correctly infer Compressor+Cooler coupling: Compressor P_out determines the bubble-point window that Cooler T_out must hit.

name: BTX two-stage sequential flash — benzene, toluene, o-xylene
description: Partially separate a ternary benzene-toluene-o-xylene mixture (33/33/33 mol%) at 25°C and 1 atm using two sequential heat-and-flash stages. First stage: heat to 95°C and flash to recover benzene-rich vapour. Second stage: heat the liquid bottoms to 125°C and flash again to separate toluene from xylene.
source: Crude BTX fractionation first two stages. Tests whether second-stage heater temperature is correctly set above toluene bp (110.6°C) but below xylene bp (144.4°C) — and whether this constraint is derived from the first-stage split, not the raw feed.
notes: Benzene bp=80.1°C, toluene bp=110.6°C, o-xylene bp=144.4°C. HT-01 targets above benzene bp; HT-02 must target above toluene bp independently. PR or SRK required. Two-stage coupling: HT-02 input composition depends entirely on VES-01 split.

name: n-Hexane–n-heptane–n-octane ternary heat-flash-cool
description: Partially separate an equimolar n-hexane, n-heptane, and n-octane mixture at 25°C and 1 atm using three units: heat to 85°C to vaporise hexane preferentially (hexane bp=69°C, heptane bp=98°C, octane bp=126°C), flash-separate in a vessel, then cool the heptane-octane-rich liquid bottoms to 30°C for product collection.
source: Naphtha pre-flash separation. Three consecutive n-alkanes with 30 K boiling-point spacing — moderate relative volatility. Tests whether PR EOS correctly handles a ternary near-ideal mixture and whether the flash temperature targets the hexane-dominant vapour fraction.
notes: n-Hexane bp=68.7°C, n-heptane bp=98.4°C, n-octane bp=125.7°C. At 85°C the feed is above hexane bp and below heptane bp — predominantly hexane vaporises. Near-ideal system: PR or SRK required, no BIPs needed.

name: Acetone-methanol heat-flash-cool-pump with azeotrope
description: Separate an acetone-methanol feed (60 mol% acetone) at 25°C and 1 atm through four units: heat to 60°C to enter the two-phase region above the 55.7°C minimum-boiling azeotrope, flash-separate in a vessel to recover acetone-enriched vapour, cool the methanol-rich liquid bottoms to 25°C, then pump to 3 bar.
source: Acetone recovery from methanol solvent mixture. Azeotrope at 55.7°C (88.5 mol% acetone) means feed at 60 mol% acetone is below the azeotropic composition — vapour is enriched toward the azeotrope from the acetone-lean side.
notes: Acetone bp=56.1°C, methanol bp=64.7°C. Min-boiling azeotrope at 55.7°C, 88.5 mol% acetone. Heater target must be above azeotrope bp (55.7°C) and below methanol bp (64.7°C) — a 9 K window. NRTL BIPs critical; Raoult's Law predicts no azeotrope.

name: Chloroform-methanol heat-flash-cool with minimum-boiling azeotrope
description: Partially separate a chloroform and methanol mixture (50 mol% chloroform) at 25°C and 1 atm using three units: heat to 57°C to enter the two-phase region above the 53.4°C minimum-boiling azeotrope (87 mol% chloroform), flash-separate to recover chloroform-enriched vapour, then cool the methanol-rich liquid bottoms to 25°C.
source: Chloroform-methanol azeotropic mixture arising from pharmaceutical solvent recovery. Negative deviations from Raoult's Law (strong CHCl3–MeOH H-bonding) produce a minimum-boiling azeotrope at a temperature BELOW both pure component boiling points.
notes: CHCl3 bp=61.2°C, MeOH bp=64.7°C, azeotrope at 53.4°C (87 mol% CHCl3). Heater target must exceed azeotrope bp (53.4°C) but stay below CHCl3 bp (61.2°C) — a 7.8 K window. Negative deviations make this a thermodynamic stress test for NRTL BIP accuracy.

name: Acetonitrile-water two-stage heat-flash enrichment
description: Enrich an acetonitrile-water feed (40 mol% acetonitrile) at 25°C and 1 atm using a two-stage sequential heat-and-flash process. First stage: heat to 82°C and flash in the first vessel. Second stage: heat the acetonitrile-depleted liquid bottoms to 95°C and flash in a second vessel to recover residual acetonitrile. The acetonitrile-water azeotrope (76.5°C, 83 mol% MeCN) limits maximum single-stage enrichment.
source: Acetonitrile recovery from aqueous pharmaceutical waste. Two-stage flash exploits the fact that below the azeotrope composition (83% MeCN) each flash step enriches the vapour in MeCN. Second-stage heater target depends on the composition leaving VES-01, creating strong inter-stage coupling.
notes: MeCN bp=82°C, water bp=100°C, azeotrope at 76.5°C (83 mol% MeCN). At 40 mol% MeCN feed, both flash stages operate below the azeotrope composition so vapour is always MeCN-enriched. HT-02 temperature is fully determined by the VES-01 split — repair loop must resolve this dependency.

name: Diethyl ether-methanol heat-flash-cool with azeotrope
description: Separate a diethyl ether and methanol mixture (50 mol% ether) at 20°C and 1 atm: heat to 40°C to operate above the 32.4°C minimum-boiling azeotrope (90 mol% ether) and vaporise the ether-rich phase, flash-separate in a vessel, then cool the methanol-rich liquid bottoms to 15°C for collection.
source: Ether-methanol solvent separation in pharmaceutical manufacturing. Near-ambient azeotrope (32.4°C) in a highly flammable system — tests whether ParamMapper targets the narrow T window (32.4–34.6°C) rather than a generic ambient-temperature default.
notes: DEE bp=34.6°C, MeOH bp=64.7°C, azeotrope at 32.4°C (90 mol% DEE). Feed at 50 mol% DEE is far below the azeotropic composition — vapour is strongly enriched in DEE. Heater target must exceed azeotrope bp by at least 7 K but the range is very narrow (32.4 to 34.6°C for DEE bp).

name: Ethyl acetate–ethanol–water five-unit ternary separation
description: Process a ternary feed of ethyl acetate (50 mol%), ethanol (30 mol%), and water (20 mol%) at 25°C and 1 atm through five units. Heat to 80°C, flash in the first vessel to recover ethyl-acetate-rich vapour. Cool the vapour to 50°C to partially recondense it, flash in the second vessel for further enrichment. Pump the water-rich liquid from the first vessel to 5 bar for downstream aqueous treatment.
source: Ethyl acetate purification from fermentation broth — a classic ternary azeotrope system with three binary azeotropes: EtOAc/EtOH (71.8°C), EtOAc/water (70.4°C heterogeneous), and EtOH/water (78.1°C). All three BIP pairs are in the corpus.
notes: Three binary azeotropes in one system: EtOAc/EtOH (71.8°C, 54% EtOAc), EtOAc/water (70.4°C heterogeneous), EtOH/water (78.1°C, 89.4%). BIPs required for all three pairs: EtOAc/EtOH ✓, EtOAc/water ✓, EtOH/water ✓. Five-unit split topology with parallel paths stresses both BIP injection and repair loop.
skip_reason: three-phase LLE not supported in current wrapper — EtOAc/water heterogeneous azeotrope requires VLLE which NestedLoops flash cannot resolve

name: Cyclohexane-ethanol heat-flash-cool-pump with near-azeotrope
description: Partially separate a cyclohexane and ethanol mixture (50 mol% cyclohexane) at 25°C and 1 atm: heat to 70°C to enter the two-phase region above the minimum-boiling azeotrope (64.9°C, 54.5 mol% cyclohexane), flash in a vessel to separate cyclohexane-rich vapour from ethanol-rich liquid, cool the liquid bottoms to 30°C, then pump to 4 bar.
source: Cyclohexane recovery from ethanol extraction process. Feed at 50 mol% CyHex sits just below the azeotrope (54.5% CyHex). Heater must target above azeotrope bp (64.9°C) but result is limited by proximity to the azeotrope — tests whether the system correctly applies the near-azeotrope guard in separation_achieved.
notes: CyHex bp=80.7°C, EtOH bp=78.4°C. Min-boiling azeotrope at 64.9°C, 54.5 mol% CyHex. Feed at 50% CyHex is below azeotrope — vapor enriched toward 54.5%. Separation limited to ~8% relative difference due to near-azeotrope VLE. BIP: cyclohexane/ethanol ✓.

name: Ethanol–n-heptane five-unit two-stage flash train
description: Separate an ethanol and n-heptane feed (40 mol% ethanol) at 25°C and 1 atm through a five-unit two-stage sequence. Heat to 82°C to partially vaporise the ethanol-rich phase, flash in the first vessel. Route the ethanol-rich vapour through a cooler to 35°C to partially recondense, then flash in the second vessel for further enrichment. Pump the heptane-rich liquid from the first vessel to 5 bar.
source: Ethanol-hydrocarbon liquid-liquid extraction pre-treatment. Strong positive deviations from Raoult's Law (ethanol/heptane are nearly immiscible at room temperature) drive a VLE minimum-boiling azeotrope near 71-72°C. Five-unit split topology with split-path flow exercises both BIP injection and multi-unit repair coupling.
notes: EtOH bp=78.4°C, n-heptane bp=98.4°C. BIP: ethanol/n-heptane ✓. Azeotrope near 71-72°C at ~24 mol% EtOH. Feed at 40 mol% EtOH is above azeotrope composition — vapour is heptane-enriched in this regime. COOL-01 target at 35°C must keep VES-02 feed in two-phase region. Strong five-unit coupling expected to require 3+ repair iterations.
